title: 1979 AHSME Problem 26
statement: The function \(f\) satisfies the functional equation \[ f(x)+f(y)=f(x+y)-xy-1 \] for every pair \(x,\) \(y\) of real numbers. If \(f(1)=1,\) then the number of integers \(n\ne1\) for which \(f(n)=n\) is

solutions.text:
Setting \(x=1\) gives \(f(y+1)-f(y)=y+2.\) Setting \(x=y=0\) gives \(f(0)=-1.\) Extending the recurrence in both directions yields, for every integer \(n,\) \[ f(n)=\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2}. \] Thus \(f(n)=n\) is equivalent to \[ \begin{aligned} n^2+n-2&=(n+2)(n-1)\\ &=0. \end{aligned} \] The integer solutions are \(n=-2\) and \(n=1,\) and after excluding \(1\) exactly one remains.

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Set one variable equal to \(1\) to get a recurrence for consecutive integer inputs
Find \(f(0)\), solve the recurrence for all integers, and then impose \(f(n)=n\)
